title: 20 Simple, Low Stress Ideas for Boosting Teacher Credibility
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Stuart lays out his Care-Competence-Passion (CCP) credibility framework as an organizing structure for twenty concrete, low-effort classroom moves, five under each of passion, urgency (which he treats as a subset of passion), care, and competence. The passion ideas focus on verbally signaling appreciation and enthusiasm for the material — mini-sermons, 'nerding out' over student work, and naming that some content won't be practically useful but is still worth learning. The urgency ideas use countdowns, procedural reteaching, and authoritative presence practice to signal that classroom time matters. The care ideas center on systematic connection (the clipboard-tracking system, prioritizing standoffish students, daily positive parent messages), and the competence ideas emphasize fast feedback turnaround, John Woodenizing behaviors down to granular detail, and following through on small commitments. He closes by reassuring readers that the list isn't a checklist to complete in full but a menu, and that the underlying work is meant to be approached playfully.
points: Stuart organizes twenty tactics under his CCP (Care, Competence, Passion) credibility model, making the list a practical index for the broader theory rather than a random grab-bag of tips.

He reframes 'passion' partly as urgency — physical and verbal signals (countdowns, 'this work is important because...') that classroom time is finite and worth protecting, distinct from raw enthusiasm.

The care section explicitly names the instinct problem it's solving: teachers naturally connect with easy or already-flagged students first, so the fix is a mechanical tracking system plus a deliberate 'standoffish students first' rule.

On competence, same-day or next-day feedback turnaround and 'John Woodenizing' a behavior (teaching it down to granular detail) are offered as concrete substitutes for vague exhortations to 'give good feedback' or 'have high expectations.'
quotes: As I've said, I think any classroom where a teacher is consistently signaling CCP — Care, Competence, and Passion — to each student is a classroom where the teacher will be increasingly credible.

Just say sometimes, "Nope — you probably won't use this someday. In fact, I'd be shocked if you did. BUT it's still so awesome! I'm so glad we get to learn about it together!" Be relentless with this kind of thinking.
We're not counting down because we want to be done — at least, most of the time we're not! We're counting down to recognize the reality that our lives are finite and there's much to be made of them.
Don't trust yourself to regularly create moments of genuine connection with students. Instead, print off all the names of your students and put them on a clipboard. Let the clipboard keep you honest!
It's easy for lots of us (me included) to mostly connect with students on a personal level. But credible teachers make clear to each student that that student's growth as a learner matters to them.
This work is fun — at its core, that's what it is. This work is good and powerful — strip it all the way down, and that's all that you'll find.
